title: 7-round AES-128: Online/data/memory tradeoff: selected subkeys

target.description: Reduced 7-round AES-128 with whitening k_-1, final MixColumns omitted, and u_i=MC^-1(k_i). Selected round-key material as in the parallel/altered stage; n controls retained-table coverage. Selected-subkey goal is distinct from master-key recovery.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES schedule; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key subset is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: Retain2^-n of the special table and repeat with2^n more delta-sets. Source writes n>=0; finite128-bit input space imposes n<=25 as a necessary fresh-data constraint, not a sufficiency proof.
assumptions: The four-round one-byte differential is modeled at2^-120; Observation5 enumerates middle states using an average S-box count.
Wrong-key multisets are modeled random. The journal's separate probability proof has documented count/max-probability issues.
Reported time is the online stage; preprocessing is explicit and key-independent. Partial-encryption conversion factors are author estimates.

time.note: Online stage only; complete-key headlines do not individually price the remaining-key search.

data.note: Expected pair collection and retained-table coverage under the source assumptions.

memory.note: Special-multiset table: approximately512 bits per entry.

preprocessing.note: Source base2^127×2^8×2^-3=2^132; retained-table factor2^-n. Canonicalization, sorting and auxiliary-table overheads are not fully itemized.

success.description: The journal does not quantify overall recovery success for this exact endpoint. Preserve its recovery scope and source-native resource budget; no probability is borrowed from another AES variant, tradeoff, or the2010 proceedings. The n=13 table fraction and additional delta-sets compensate in expected work; they do not establish finite-budget success. The existing average-versus-uniform middle-state enumeration issue and the documented original multiset-proof limitations remain.

review.scope: Exact26-page journal edition, separately from the proceedings. No probability was added: Sections6.1–6.4 do not quantify recovery at the n=13 sampled-table budget; Section5.2.2 gives a wrong-guess estimate for2^64.5 data before changing the endpoint to2^64.43. No earlier-budget or other-edition success is transplanted. Existing multiset, notation, cost and correctness obligations remain; not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: PDF12/13: source random-permutation expectation for the one-byte-output four-round core. It is not experimentally checked; parallel byte choices and a larger input structure do not give independent trials.
PDF19 Section6.1 PhaseAii and Section6.2: the96-bit initial pair sieve remains in the modified construction. A local wrong-pair model, not aggregate success.

PDF21 Section6.4: retain a2^-n fraction of the table at the exact balanced pointn=13, then use2^n more delta-sets. A retained-table fraction is not the probability a right multiset is included without a distribution assumption.

evidence.interpretation: Full source version read and compared. Matching statements share one scoped record; changed claims and source-specific discrepancies retain their own identities.

field_conflicts.label: Average solution count versus asserted uniform enumeration bound
field_conflicts.description: Observation5 uses one S-box solution on average to assert an at-most2^64 middle-state count. Its own footnote gives0/2/4 solutions. The mean does not by itself prove the stated bound for every structured difference tuple; the global count remains under review.
